items.context: The release-record research (Finding 7) proposes two tables — `releases` (one row per release event) plus `release_platforms` (one row per platform per release). Round 1's plan sketch used a single `release_records` table with JSON-ish platforms. The two shapes are not equivalent for query patterns (per-platform status updates, partial failures, joining to approvals) and should be settled before Phase 1 is coded.

options.label: Adopt the research's two-table schema verbatim (`releases` + `release_platforms`)
options.rationale: Normalized: per-platform status updates, direct FK to `deployment_approvals`, clean indexes on status. Matches the research we already ran and the migration numbering (004). Supports future promotion via `promoted_from_release_id` without schema changes.

options.label: Single `releases` table with JSONB `platforms` column
options.rationale: One table to maintain. Good for read-heavy views. Weaker for partial updates (must rewrite the JSONB blob per-platform state change) and loses relational integrity with `deployment_approvals`. Adds friction for the re-verify endpoint that needs per-platform writes.

options.label: Extend existing `published_versions` table instead of adding new ones
options.rationale: Reuses an existing table. But `published_versions` is deployment-scoped, not release-event-scoped. Bending it to carry release-event semantics mixes concerns and breaks the research's conceptual separation (release event vs. deployed artifact row).

items.topic: Authentication on LPBS's new POST /api/v1/deploy-readiness endpoint
items.context: D2=A in round 1 added a new HTTP endpoint in LPBS. LPBS has three established auth models: `requireAdmin` (set-current), `requireAdminOrService` (presign/commit/apply — shared service secret), and per-app `X-Update-Key` (public update manifests). Each has different blast radius and operator ergonomics. DM is a trusted sibling service, so per-app keys are over-scoped; public keys are under-scoped.

options.label: Admin-only (`requireAdmin`) — DM uses admin bearer token
options.rationale: Safest. Matches set-current's level of trust. But forces DM to hold an admin secret for LPBS, which is broader privilege than strictly needed for a readiness check.

options.label: Admin-or-Service (`requireAdminOrService`) — DM uses LPBS_SERVICE_SECRET
options.rationale: Matches the pattern S2D already uses for presign/commit/apply. DM becomes a peer service, no new secret. Readiness check is read-only and has the same trust level as publish — if a service can publish, it can certainly ask 'am I ready to publish'.

options.label: Per-app `X-Update-Key` (the same header used for public manifests)
options.rationale: Reuses existing per-app keys. But those keys are read-mostly and meant for update clients, not for a trusted service readiness check. Semantically wrong layer.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe an alternative auth model (e.g., mTLS, new DM-specific service token).

items.topic: Channel promotion scope for this item
items.context: Research Finding 6 specifies a formal channel model: nightly → beta → stable, with promote semantics (a new release row pointing at `promoted_from_release_id`, inheriting commit + artifacts but targeting a higher channel). This item is already L-effort; adding a promote API+CLI+UI would push it toward XL and duplicate the skill-retargeting work.

options.label: Defer all promotion work; support only the `stable` channel end-to-end in this item
options.rationale: Matches today's real-world flow (we don't currently ship nightly/beta). Keeps this item L. Schema still includes `channel` and `promoted_from_release_id` so the follow-up is pure handler/CLI/UI work.

options.label: Defer promote API+CLI+UI to a follow-up, but ensure the schema and orchestrator handle arbitrary channel values
options.rationale: Pragmatic middle ground. An operator can release to any channel by passing `--channel beta`. Promote flow (creating a promoted copy) is a follow-up item. This validates the channel model without the extra UI/CLI work.

options.label: Fully in scope: implement promote endpoint, CLI verb (`releases promote <id> --to <channel>`), and UI action in this item
options.rationale: Highest completeness. But inflates the item significantly and delays the orchestration win. The research already maps out what promote needs; doing it later is low-risk.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe an alternative scope for channel promotion.

items.topic: Concurrency guard for simultaneous release-starts on the same profile
items.context: Two `POST /profiles/{id}/releases/start` calls could hit DM at the same time for the same profile. The research schema adds `UNIQUE(profile_id, git_commit_hash, channel)` which prevents duplicate records for the SAME commit+channel, but doesn't prevent two in-flight releases on different commits from stomping on each other mid-orchestration (both calling into LPBS, both trying to set `set-current`, etc.). We need an explicit concurrency story.

options.label: Rely only on the UNIQUE constraint (`profile_id, git_commit_hash, channel`); let 409 Conflict surface on duplicate
options.rationale: Simplest. Zero new code. Catches the most common misuse (double-submit of the same release). But does NOT serialize concurrent releases for different commits to the same profile — two operators racing different commits could both reach the LPBS publish step.

options.label: Postgres advisory lock at profile scope via `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('release:' || profile_id))` for the duration of orchestration; 409 on lock contention
options.rationale: Serializes releases per profile. Second caller gets a fast 409 with a clear message. Advisory locks are lightweight (no table lock) and release automatically on transaction end or connection drop. Matches how DB-backed job queues handle this.

options.label: Application-level mutex (in-memory lock per profile_id, held by the orchestrator goroutine)
options.rationale: Works in single-node DM. Breaks if DM is ever scaled horizontally. Not worth the tradeoff given the Postgres advisory lock is equally simple and multi-node-safe.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe an alternative concurrency strategy (queue-based serialization, optimistic status transition, etc.).

items.text: The release-record research (Finding 9) confirms the S2D pipeline already carries Config.Version → ReleaseVersion and Provenance.GitCommitHash through to LPBS upload. Phase 5 in the plan only needs to add ReleaseID and Channel to the plumbing — the rest is existing code. This shrinks the S2D-side change from 'new data pipeline' to 'two new fields threaded through existing structs' and should keep Phase 5 under a day of work.

Section 8 Contract Decisions moved D1-D6 to Settled and added D7-D10 as the new TBDs. Section 9 Testing Plan added dry-run exclusion, concurrency, verification hard-fail, and LPBS deploy-readiness integration tests. Section 11 Risks added concurrency, orphan-record, auth, and promotion-forward-compat entries. Section 12 Non-goals explicitly excludes promote API/UI, dedicated /releases page, and published_unverified status.
